product_backlog.title: Core To-Do App Features
product_backlog.description: Core To-Do List and Task Management functionality

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Enables organizing tasks into separate lists.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the main page, When they enter a list name and click create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.title: Create To-Do List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified list creation feature meets all acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list exists, When the user adds a task with a description, Then the task appears in that list.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short description so that I know what needs to be done.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows tracking individual items within a list.
product_backlog.title: Add Task to List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short description so that I know what needs to be done.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified acceptance criteria for US-0002: users can successfully add tasks to a list and view them on the main page.

product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track progress.
product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists, When the user marks it as complete or incomplete, Then its completion state updates and is visually reflected.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track progress.

product_backlog.title: Delete Task
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Keeps the list clean of unwanted tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists, When the user clicks delete on the task, Then the task is removed from the list.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.

product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete lists.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows removing whole lists and associated tasks at once.
acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list exists, When the user deletes the list, Then the list and all its contained tasks are removed.
product_backlog.title: Delete Entire List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete lists.

product_backlog.title: View All Lists and Tasks
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all my lists and tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a clear overview.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Provides clear visibility into all created lists and tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has lists and tasks, When they view the home page, Then all lists and their tasks are displayed with completed tasks visually distinguished.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists and tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a clear overview.

messages.content: [SPRINT PHASE: Plan & Start Sprint] The Ready backlog is deep enough - Scrum Master calls start_sprint(goal) if that hasn't happened yet this sprint, then Product Owner publishes it via create_sprint_backlog_pr(). More backlog grooming belongs here only for a specific, stated reason, not as a default.

This is sprint 2 of 5. Continue the product vision from before - check the existing repo content (specs/, code, .hc/state.json) before planning, so you build on what's already there rather than repeating or contradicting it. As before: the sprint goal and backlog are pre-approved. Start by calling start_sprint(goal) to officially kick off this sprint - it mechanically resets the sprint's own token/event budget, so skipping it leaves this sprint silently running on whatever budget the previous sprint already spent. Then proceed directly through planning, development, PR creation, CI verification, sprint review (create_sprint_report), and the release PR (create_release_pr) without waiting for further approval. Do not ask me anything else during this sprint.

framework_change_proposals.rationale: Set up Python and Flask development workbench with pytest for testing and Flask for the web app implementation.
framework_change_proposals.workbench_setup_script:
#!/bin/sh
# Development Workbench: python-flask (US-0022, EP-0010)
#
# Toolchain for scaffolding, developing, testing, running, and debugging a
# Flask application inside the agent image. The base agent image
# (agent.Dockerfile, FROM python:3.11-slim) already provides Python 3.11 +
# pip, so this script only layers the Flask-stack-specific packages on top
# - the same "only add what the base image doesn't already have" shape
# every Development Workbench template follows.
set -e

pip install --no-cache-dir \
    flask \
    pytest \
    pytest-flask \
    debugpy \
    httpie

cat <<'EOF'
python-flask workbench ready: flask, pytest, pytest-flask, debugpy, httpie installed.

Scaffold (minimal app, from the project root):
  mkdir -p app && cat > app/__init__.py <<'PY'
  from flask import Flask

  app = Flask(__name__)

  @app.route("/")
  def index():
      return "ok"
  PY

Install project-declared deps:
  pip install -r requirements.txt

Test:
  pytest

Run:
  flask --app app run --debug --host=0.0.0.0

Debug (attach a remote debugger on port 5678):
  python -m debugpy --listen 0.0.0.0:5678 --wait-for-client \
      -m flask --app app run --no-debugger --no-reload

Exploratory testing:
  http GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/     # HTTPie against the running dev server
  flask --app app shell               # interactive REPL with full app context
EOF
